answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks by anchoring identities to ambient seismic resonance. Nodes record ground vibrations via a quartz geophone anchored into bedrock, such as a limestone karst or river terrace. An attacker must deploy discrete sensors across distinct geological sites per identity, incurring substantial equipment and land-leasing costs. However, seasonal soil moisture shifts alter wave velocity, degrading correlation fidelity and intermittently rejecting valid nodes.
